title: Maps out of a simplex boundary represent the proper-face limit
statement:
Let $T:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ be a small simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and let $n\geq0$. Define $\Delta^n_r=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([r],[n])$ and let $\partial\Delta^n_r$ consist of the nonsurjective order-preserving maps $[r]\to[n]$, with operators given by precomposition. In particular $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Let $F_n(T)$ be the set of families $(x_\iota)$ with $x_\iota\in T_k$ for each proper injective order-preserving map $\iota:[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$, $k<n$, satisfying $T(\theta)x_\iota=x_{\iota\theta}$ whenever $\theta:[l]\hookrightarrow[k]$ is injective. The restriction map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\partial\Delta^n,T)\longrightarrow F_n(T),\qquad h\longmapsto(h_k(\iota))_\iota$$
is a bijection, natural in $T$. Equivalently these evaluations exhibit this Hom set as the limit in sets of the diagram with one copy of $T_k$ for each proper injection $\iota:[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$ and, for each injective order-preserving $\theta:[l]\hookrightarrow[k]$, the map $T(\theta)$ from the copy of $T_k$ indexed by $\iota$ to the copy of $T_l$ indexed by $\iota\theta$. Under this bijection, restriction of the map $\Delta^n\to T$ given by $z\in T_n$ corresponds to $(T(\iota)z)_\iota$. The case $n=0$ gives a singleton on each side, the empty-family limit.

proof.text: Precomposition preserves nonsurjectivity, since the image of $\alpha\theta$ is contained in the image of $\alpha$. Thus the stated boundary is a simplicial subset, with morphisms interpreted as natural transformations by [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. If $n=0$, every map $[r]\to[0]$ is surjective because $[r]$ is nonempty. The boundary is empty in every degree, so there is exactly one map from it to $T$. There are no proper injections into $[0]$, so $F_0(T)$ consists of the unique empty family. All asserted compatibilities and the empty-limit universal property are then automatic. Henceforth assume $n\geq1$. For any $h:\partial\Delta^n\to T$ put $R(h)_\iota=h_k(\iota)$. Naturality gives $T(\theta)h_k(\iota)=h_l(\iota\theta)$ for every injective $\theta:[l]\to[k]$, so $R(h)\in F_n(T)$.

source.place: Tag 08NK (section-trivial-kan), boundary paragraph; Tag 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), restriction to face evaluations; the n=0 case is checked directly

proof.text: Fix $x=(x_\iota)\in F_n(T)$. Write $\delta_i^n:[n-1]\hookrightarrow[n]$ for the injection omitting $i$. For every nonsurjective $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$, choose a vertex $i$ outside its image. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization] there is a unique order-preserving $\psi_i:[r]\to[n-1]$ such that $\alpha=\delta_i^n\psi_i$. Associate to this choice the candidate value $T(\psi_i)x_{\delta_i^n}\in T_r$. There is no bound on $r$ in the factorization lemma. The next step checks that this value is independent of the omitted vertex, so this prescription will define $H(x)_r(\alpha)$.

source.place: Tag 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), construction f_alpha = U(psi) f_i; extended to every r because only nonsurjectivity is used

proof.text:
Suppose $i<j$ are both missing from the image of $\alpha$. The nonempty image of $[r]$ leaves at most one vertex missing when $n=1$, so this case requires $n\geq2$. In $\alpha=\delta_i^n\psi_i$, the value $j-1$ is missing from $\psi_i$, since $\delta_i^n(j-1)=j$ and $\delta_i^n$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization] again to get $\psi_i=\delta_{j-1}^{n-1}\xi$ with $\xi:[r]\to[n-2]$. The identity in [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity], with its parameter $n-1\geq1$, gives
$$\gamma:=\delta_i^n\delta_{j-1}^{n-1}=\delta_j^n\delta_i^{n-1}.$$
Consequently $\alpha=\delta_j^n\delta_i^{n-1}\xi$, and uniqueness of factorization through $\delta_j^n$ gives $\psi_j=\delta_i^{n-1}\xi$. The map $\gamma:[n-2]\hookrightarrow[n]$ is a proper injection. Compatibility of $x$ for its two injective factorizations, and contravariant functoriality of $T$, yield
$$T(\psi_i)x_{\delta_i^n}=T(\xi)T(\delta_{j-1}^{n-1})x_{\delta_i^n}=T(\xi)x_\gamma=T(\xi)T(\delta_i^{n-1})x_{\delta_j^n}=T(\psi_j)x_{\delta_j^n}.$$
Equal choices coincide by uniqueness, and reversed choices reduce to this calculation. This proves independence and defines $H(x)_r$ in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), independence of the choice (i,psi); Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), first identity

proof.text:
For an arbitrary order-preserving $\theta:[s]\to[r]$ and a boundary simplex $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$, take a vertex $i$ missing from $\alpha$. It is also missing from $\alpha\theta$. If $\alpha=\delta_i^n\psi_i$, then $\alpha\theta=\delta_i^n(\psi_i\theta)$; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization] identifies the factor for this choice of $i$. Using choice independence from step 3 and functoriality,
$$H(x)_s(\alpha\theta)=T(\psi_i\theta)x_{\delta_i^n}=T(\theta)T(\psi_i)x_{\delta_i^n}=T(\theta)H(x)_r(\alpha).$$
Thus $H(x)$ is a morphism of simplicial sets, including naturality for degeneracy operators, not just face maps.

source.place: Tag 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), verification f_{alpha psi} = U(psi) f_alpha; no restriction on source degrees is needed

proof.text: For a proper injection $\iota:[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$, take $i$ missing from its image and write $\iota=\delta_i^n\psi$. The final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization] says that $\psi$ is injective. Since $x$ is compatible under all injective operators, $H(x)_k(\iota)=T(\psi)x_{\delta_i^n}=x_\iota$. Hence $R(H(x))=x$, including components at every lower-dimensional proper face.

source.place: Tag 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), inverse constructions; the statement here retains evaluations at all proper injections

proof.text:
Conversely, for any $h:\partial\Delta^n\to T$ and $\alpha=\delta_i^n\psi$ as above, naturality of $h$ at $\psi$ gives
$$H(R(h))_r(\alpha)=T(\psi)R(h)_{\delta_i^n}=T(\psi)h_{n-1}(\delta_i^n)=h_r(\delta_i^n\psi)=h_r(\alpha).$$
Equality on every simplex in every degree is equality of the natural transformations. Therefore $H(R(h))=h$, which together with step 5 proves the claimed bijection.

source.place: Tag 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), mutually inverse bijections, with the omitted verification written explicitly

proof.text: Let $u:T\to T'$ be a morphism of simplicial sets. The componentwise assignment $F_n(u)(x)_\iota=u_k(x_\iota)$ preserves compatibility, because $u_lT(\theta)=T'(\theta)u_k$. Evaluation gives $R(u\circ h)_\iota=u_k(h_k(\iota))=F_n(u)(R(h))_\iota$, proving naturality in $T$. For $z\in T_n$, define $a_z:\Delta^n\to T$ by $(a_z)_r(\alpha)=T(\alpha)z$. Functoriality makes this a natural transformation. Conversely any $a:\Delta^n\to T$ satisfies $a_r(\alpha)=T(\alpha)a_n(\mathrm{id}_{[n]})$ by naturality, so this is exactly the map given by $z$. Its boundary restriction evaluates at $\iota$ as $T(\iota)z$, proving the last asserted formula.

source.place: Tag 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), functoriality; Tag 0177 (lemma-simplex-map), whose evaluation argument is written out here

proof.text: The index diagram is small and finite: its objects are proper injections into the fixed finite ordered set $[n]$, and its arrows are injective maps $\theta$ as in the statement. Identities and composition are those of order-preserving maps, and the diagram laws are the functor laws for $T$. Its arrows point from $\iota$ to $\iota\theta$, giving $T_k\to T_l$ as required. The coordinate evaluations $p_\iota(x)=x_\iota$ define a cone with apex $F_n(T)$. Given any set $W$ with compatible maps $f_\iota:W\to T_k$, the function $f:W\to F_n(T)$ defined by $f(w)=(f_\iota(w))_\iota$ is well-defined by that compatibility and satisfies $p_\iota f=f_\iota$. It is the unique such function, by equality of coordinates. This proves the limit universal property directly. Transporting these coordinate maps along $R$ proves that the evaluations on $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\partial\Delta^n,T)$ exhibit that set as the asserted limit. Step 1 already proves the empty-diagram case $n=0$.
